concept: Sum of an infinite geometric series
prompt:
**(a)** Find the sum to infinity of $12+8+\dfrac{16}{3}+\dots$ **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why $1+1.1+1.21+\dots$ has no sum to infinity. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $r=\dfrac{8}{12}=\dfrac23$ **(A1)**; $S_\infty=\dfrac{12}{1-\frac23}=36$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $r=1.1$ and $|r|\ge1$, so the terms do not shrink and the partial sums grow without bound. **(R1)**

prompt:
Consider the geometric series $1+(2x-1)+(2x-1)^{2}+\dots$

**(a)** Find the values of $x$ for which the series converges. **[2]**

**(b)** Find an expression for the sum to infinity in terms of $x$. **[1]**

**(c)** Find $x$ given that the sum to infinity is 2. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $|2x-1|<1$ **(M1)** $\iff 0<x<1$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $S_\infty=\dfrac{1}{1-(2x-1)}=\dfrac{1}{2-2x}$ **(A1)**

**(c)** $\dfrac{1}{2-2x}=2 \Rightarrow 2-2x=\tfrac12$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow x=\tfrac34$, which lies in $0<x<1$ **(A1)**

Always check that the value found satisfies the convergence condition.
